text:
alice: Heads-up — we need to settle the tiling vs projection contract before we start the dashboard refactor. Quick proposal below, want opinions + rollout ideas.

ben: can you summarize the core tradeoffs you're seeing?

alice: sure. Two schools:
1) Projection-first: projection layer performs RBAC and returns fully-authorized tile payloads (easy for frontend, higher cache variance).
2) Tiling-first: tiler returns canonical tiles and the projection layer applies viewer-scoped filtering/authorization (better cache reuse across tenants, projection does more work).

carla: leaning toward tiling-first. If tiles are canonical (no user bits), we can cache heavily at the CDN/edge. RBAC pushdown into projection lets us memoize render outputs for common roles.

ben: worry is extra latency on the hot path — projection would need fast auth lookups. Do we have an existing fast auth cache?

dana: we have the tenant role cache in memcached + local LRU on servers. Typical auth check is O(1) after warmup. Biggest source of latency will be rehydrating tile state + any remote feature flags.

eric: another angle — make the contract explicit: tiler returns tiles with a small metadata envelope that projection can use to short-circuit RBAC when possible. Eg: `tile.metadata.public: true|false`, `tile.metadata.scope: [org|team|user]`. That avoids recomputing full checks for public tiles.

carla: yes — add a tiny auth-hint. Also include a stable tile fingerprint so projection can check a cache key: `proj_cache_key = tile.fingerprint + viewer.role_hash`.

alice: sketch of interface:
```
GET /internal/tiles/:tile_id
Response 200:
{
  "id": "t123",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:...",
  "metadata": {"scope":"org","public":false},
  "payload": { /* canonical tile data, no viewer-scoped fields */ }
}

POST /internal/projection?viewer_id=uid
Body: { "tile_ids": ["t123","t124"] }
Response 200: { "rendered": [ {"tile_id":"t123","html":"...","cache_key":"k"} ] }
```

ben: that seems reasonable. Where do we put RBAC logic exactly? Projection service owns final enforcement, but tiler must assert metadata accuracy. We need a CI check for mismatches.

dana: +1 on CI lint. We can add a unit test that simulates viewers against a tile's metadata and compares projection decision to a golden auth matrix.

eric: rollout plan idea:
- Phase 1: implement tile metadata + fingerprint in tiler, projection reads metadata but still does full auth.
- Phase 2: projection starts using hint path + cache for fast-path, telemetry enabled.
- Phase 3: progressively change tiler to mark more tiles as public/scope-limited, flip feature flag to rely on hints.
- Phase 4: run canary with 5% traffic, compare latency and cache-hit signals.

carla: metrics to watch: projection p50/p95, proj cache hit ratio, tile fingerprint churn, mismatch errors (projection denies despite hint saying public).

alice: agree. Also we need a migration story for existing dashboards: add a background job that computes fingerprints and metadata for all existing tiles.

ben: how do we handle complex tiles that depend on viewer content (e.g., "my tasks")? Those would be scope=user and can't be cached broadly. Fine as long as we mark scope correctly.

carla: Edge-case: panels with mixed sub-queries (some public, some user-only). Proposal: break into sub-tiles at tiler level so projection can stitch and cache subparts. Tradeoff: more tiles -> more overhead in tile lookup.

dana: implementation note: tiler should emit `subtiles: [{id, fingerprint, metadata}]` when it detects mixed privacy. That keeps projection simple.

eric: security note: projection must always fallback to authoritative auth service if `viewer.role_hash` missing or stale. No hint can bypass enforcement.

alice: action items:
- ben: prototype fingerprint+metadata in tiler (spike this week).
- carla: design CI lint for metadata vs auth matrix.
- dana: add local auth cache TTL tuning and telemetry hooks.
- eric: write canary plan + dashboards for metrics.

ben: ack. I'll post a small PR with the tiler change once the prototype is green.

deploy-bot: canary branch `tiler/meta-fingerprint` deployed to staging (build 2026.03.20-09). :rocket:

alice: thanks all — we'll regroup after the prototype results. @carla please add the CI lint issue to the console backlog. :thumbsup:
